elements.quote: Methods: Systematic review applying PRISMA guidelines.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This review assessed the impact of pre-defined selection criteria on ECPR survival.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: Adult patients (> 12 years) receiving ECPR were included.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the main inclusion criteria but does not explicitly list exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: We searched Medline, Embase, and Evidence-Based Medicine Reviews for RCTs and observational studies published from January 2000 to June 2021.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources and the date range of the search.

elements.quote: Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS).
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the method used to assess risk of bias (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale).

elements.quote: Meta-analysis and meta-regression were performed.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the methods used to synthesize the results.

elements.quote: Results: 67 studies were included: 14 prospective and 53 retrospective.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies but does not report the number of participants.

elements.quote: The number of inclusion criteria to select ECPR patients ( p = 0.292) and study design ( p = 0.962) was not associated with higher favourable neurological survival.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (association with survival).
The abstract mentions meta-analysis was performed but does not report the summary estimate or its confidence interval.

elements.quote: increased number of inclusion criteria was associated with improved outcomes
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect when groups are compared.
The abstract does not briefly summarize important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: Conclusions: Prospective studies showed number of selection criteria and, in particular, arrest to ECMO time were associated with significant improved survival. Well-designed prospective studies assessing the relative importance of criteria as well as larger efficacy studies are required to ensure appropriate application of what is a costly intervention.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their important implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Whilst promising outcomes have been reported [1-3], survival rates vary widely [3] which is likely due to differences in study design
elements.reason: Describes the current state of knowledge (varying survival rates) and important uncertainties (attributed to differences in study design).

elements.quote: However, reported outcomes vary considerably due to differing study designs and selection criteria. This review assessed the impact of pre-defined selection criteria on ECPR survival.
elements.reason: Explains the importance and need for the review by highlighting outcome variability and explicitly stating the review's objective to address this.
No mention of similar systematic reviews or explanation of the need for this review in relation to previous ones is found in the provided text.

elements.quote: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for refractory cardiac arrest (RCA, ECPR) provides adequate systemic perfusion while the underlying cause may be diagnosed and treated.
elements.reason: Briefly describes the proposed mechanism of action of the intervention (providing systemic perfusion).
No logic model or description of hypothesized relationships between intervention components and outcomes is provided in the text.

elements.quote: We used the PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome) search format: Among adults with cardiac arrest in any setting (OHCA or IHCA) who qualify for ECPR by inclusion and exclusion parameters outlined (P), does receiving ECPR, including ECMO or cardiopulmonary bypass, during cardiac arrest (I), compared to manual CPR and/or mechanical CPR (C) without any mechanical circulatory support, change meaningful outcomes (favourable neurological status or survival at study end) (O). Contemporary studies from January 2000 to June 2021 were included. Only English language studies were included. Randomised trials, non-randomised controlled trials, and observational studies (cohort studies and casecontrol studies) were included. The population included adults (age above 12) with IHCA or OHCA of any origin. Animal studies, ecological studies, case reports, reviews, abstracts, editorials, comments, and letters to the editor were excluded. Studies with ≤ 5 patients receiving ECPR or studies that did not report the inclusion or exclusion criteria regarding the eligibility of ECPR or the timing of ECPR (i.e. during or after cardiac arrest) were excluded.
elements.reason: The text explicitly specifies PICO components, eligible study designs, settings (OHCA/IHCA), and follow-outcome definitions (survival at study end).

elements.quote: Contemporary studies from January 2000 to June 2021 were included. Only English language studies were included.
elements.reason: The text specifies the dissemination year range and language restriction.
The text does not distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not being measured versus outcomes not being reported.

elements.quote: Results are reported separately for pre-defined subgroups based on type of study (retrospective or prospective), and the location of cardiac arrest (IHCA vs OHCA).
elements.reason: The text specifies the groups used for synthesis (study type, location) and links them to the analysis.
The text lists eligibility restrictions (e.g., English only, ≤5 patients) but does not provide explicit rationales for these notable restrictions.
